create.title: Actual nonzero near-resonance mass obstructs a termwise absolute twelfth-moment bound
create.statement_tex: Let Psi be fixed real even Schwartz with Psi(0)=1 and w nonzero nonnegative C_c^infinity((0,infinity)). For a_n(T)=r_2(n)n^(-3/4)Psi(sqrt(n/T)), there exist fixed0<a<b and h,c>0 such that for every sufficiently large realT, the actual coefficients are nonnegative on I_T=[aT,bT] intersect N, and T sum_(n_1,...,n_12 in I_T,0<|Delta|<=h/T) product_j a_(n_j)(T) Re w-hat(-TDelta)>=cT^(5/2), where Delta=sum_(j<=6)sqrt(n_j)-sum_(j>6)sqrt(n_j). All exact radical relations are removed using the uniform accepted absolute exact-mass bound. Consequently the full nonzero-frequency all-sign termwise absolute Fourier majorant (with prefactorT/2^12) is >=c_prime T^(5/2), so cannot be O_epsilon(T^(1+2eta+epsilon)) for everyepsilon>0 if eta<3/4. The proof uses elementary physical band mass and weighted six-root bins. For balanced2k with k>=4 the same method gives nonzero positive subsum >=c_k T^((k-1)/2); the conclusion is not asserted for k<=3 after exact deletion. This is strictly a majorant obstruction, not a lower bound for the complete signed displaced moment, and it disproves no actual moment target, M1/M2 estimate or pointwise exponent.
